value.text: Breathless on exertion, such as climbing stairs, for about two weeks; not breathless at rest.

release_text: Breathless on exertion, such as climbing stairs, for about two weeks; not breathless at rest.
lay_text: I get puffed going up the stairs, for the last couple of weeks or so. I'm fine when I'm sitting still.
rationale: Haemoglobin 72 g/L on admission, fallen from 127 g/L; exertional breathlessness is the expected symptom of an anaemia of this depth developing over weeks.

lay_text: Reading and walking, mostly.
rationale: G08: no hobby exposure. The rationale, not the answer, records that she does no shooting, soldering, stained glass, pottery glazes, fishing sinkers or furniture restoration (SPEC §6.4 rule 8).

value.text: No recent renovation, sanding or paint stripping at home; town water supply; cooks on an electric stove.

release_text: No recent renovation, sanding or paint stripping at home; town water supply; cooks on an electric stove.
lay_text: No, we haven't done any renovating or sanding, and we're on town water. I cook on an electric stove.
rationale: G08: no household source; the supplement is the only source in the article. The answer covers exactly what the item asks (renovation, paint, water, cooking fuel) and nothing more.

lay_text: I work in an office.
rationale: G08: no occupational exposure. The answer names the job only; the rationale records that office work carries no lead, battery, smelting, construction or firing-range exposure (SPEC §6.4 rule 8).

value.text: Nobody she knows has similar symptoms. The friend who gave her the herbal supplement takes the same product; she knows of no one else who takes it.

release_text: Nobody she knows has similar symptoms. The friend who gave her the herbal supplement takes the same product; she knows of no one else who takes it.
lay_text: Not that I know of. My friend who gave me the herbal capsules takes them too, but I don't know of anyone else.
rationale: ANALYSIS §6 draft; supports the public-health must-do (ask who else took it). The article does not say who else took the product. RISK for Atul: this answer mentions the supplement, so a player who asks this before a remedies question gets the supplement without the targeted question that releases H10. Alternative: answer 'Nobody I know has been unwell like this' and keep the friend for SUPPLEMENT_DETAILS.

value.text: No family history of anaemia, blood disorders or jaundice.

release_text: No family history of anaemia, blood disorders or jaundice.
lay_text: No, nobody in my family has had anaemia or blood problems or jaundice, as far as I know.
rationale: No inherited red cell disorder in this case (HPLC normal, MCV normal before admission: 93 fL at day -100 with Hb 127 g/L).

value.text: No fevers, night sweats or weight loss.

release_text: No fevers, night sweats or weight loss.
lay_text: No, no fevers or night sweats, and I haven't lost any weight.
rationale: Afebrile, CRP <0.4 mg/L, no infection (H07) and no malignancy; weight loss not reported.

value.text: Has not noticed yellowing of the eyes or skin.

release_text: Has not noticed yellowing of the eyes or skin.
lay_text: No, I haven't noticed my eyes or skin going yellow.
rationale: Bilirubin 29 umol/L on day 0, mostly unconjugated: below the level at which patients usually notice icterus. Consistent with no jaundice on examination.

value.text: No metallic taste or change in taste.

release_text: No metallic taste or change in taste.
lay_text: No, food tastes normal to me.
rationale: A classic symptom of the truth that the article does not report; SPEC §6.4 rule 2 forbids adding it, so the answer is no.

value.text: Somewhat constipated over the past few weeks; no diarrhoea; no blood in the stool.

release_text: Somewhat constipated over the past few weeks; no diarrhoea; no blood in the stool.
lay_text: I've been a bit constipated the last few weeks. No diarrhoea, and no blood.
rationale: Colicky pain with constipation is the likeliest bowel pattern for the truth, but the article does not report bowel habit. Alternative: no change. Consistent with H08 (no GI bleeding).

value.text: Poor appetite with occasional nausea; no vomiting.

release_text: Poor appetite with occasional nausea; no vomiting.
lay_text: I haven't felt much like eating, and I feel a bit sick now and then, but I haven't been sick.
rationale: Anorexia and mild nausea commonly accompany weeks of abdominal pain and lethargy; not reported by the article. No weight loss (see the fever, sweats and weight item).

value.text: Has not noticed dark or red urine.

release_text: Has not noticed dark or red urine.
lay_text: No, my wee looks normal, not dark or red.
rationale: Urinary haemosiderin not detected (L22) and haemolysis is extravascular in pattern; unconjugated bilirubin does not reach urine. No dark urine.

value.text: Periods lighter and less regular over the past year; not heavy; no bleeding between periods.

release_text: Periods lighter and less regular over the past year; not heavy; no bleeding between periods.
lay_text: My periods have got lighter and a bit irregular this last year. They're not heavy, and I don't bleed in between.
rationale: At 49, perimenopausal cycles are likeliest; not heavy, because iron studies are replete (ferritin 165 ug/L) and the anaemia is not from blood loss.

value.text: Feels tired and mentally foggy; no confusion; no headaches; mood otherwise fine.

release_text: Feels tired and mentally foggy; no confusion; no headaches; mood otherwise fine.
lay_text: I feel tired and a bit foggy in my head. I'm not confused, I haven't had headaches, and my mood's all right.
rationale: Fatigue and poor concentration fit the anaemia and progressive lethargy (H06). No encephalopathic features at this blood level; the article reports none.

value.text: No numbness, tingling or pins and needles.

release_text: No numbness, tingling or pins and needles.
lay_text: No, no numbness or tingling anywhere.
rationale: IBM spares sensation; the neuropathy of the truth is motor when present, and the article reports none.

value.text: Long-standing weakness of the grip and thighs from her inclusion body myositis, no worse recently; no new weakness.

release_text: Long-standing weakness of the grip and thighs from her inclusion body myositis, no worse recently; no new weakness.
lay_text: My grip and my thigh muscles have been weak for years because of the myositis. That hasn't changed lately, and nothing else has gone weak.
rationale: G05: IBM pattern (finger flexors, quadriceps), unchanged. The rationale records no wrist or foot drop; the answer does not name them (SPEC §6.4 rule 8).

value.text: Diffuse, crampy abdominal pain that comes and goes, worse over the past week; not related to meals; does not spread elsewhere; up to about 6/10 at its worst.

release_text: Diffuse, crampy abdominal pain that comes and goes, worse over the past week; not related to meals; does not spread elsewhere; up to about 6/10 at its worst.
lay_text: It's all over my tummy, crampy, and it comes and goes. It's been worse this past week. It's not to do with eating and it doesn't go anywhere else. At its worst maybe 6 out of 10.
rationale: Article: worsening abdominal pain for three weeks (H05). Colicky, poorly localised pain without peritonism is the likeliest pattern for the truth; character and severity are not reported.

value.text: Maintenance IVIG every four weeks for several years for inclusion body myositis; last infusion about two weeks before admission.

release_text: Maintenance IVIG every four weeks for several years for inclusion body myositis; last infusion about two weeks before admission.
lay_text: I have the immunoglobulin drip every four weeks, and have for years. The last one was about two weeks ago.
rationale: G06: long-term IVIG (H03); a recent infusion fits IgG 14.9 g/L near the upper limit, CMV and parvovirus IgG positivity and a weak IgG-only DAT from passive antibody in a group A patient.

value.text: Mycophenolate mofetil 1 g twice daily, started about six weeks before admission.

release_text: Mycophenolate mofetil 1 g twice daily, started about six weeks before admission.
lay_text: I started mycophenolate about six weeks ago, 1 gram twice a day.
rationale: G07: 'recently started' (H04); 1 g twice daily is the usual dose. Six weeks puts the start just before the symptoms began, keeping drug-related anaemia a fair alternative, while the reticulocytosis argues against marrow suppression.

value.text: Two pregnancies, both uncomplicated vaginal deliveries; no previous blood transfusions.

release_text: Two pregnancies, both uncomplicated vaginal deliveries; no previous blood transfusions.
lay_text: I have two children, both normal deliveries. I have never had a blood transfusion.
rationale: Atul to set the number of pregnancies (the draft answer is no previous transfusions). Pregnancies and transfusions are the usual sources of alloantibodies; the antibody screen is negative (L16), so any number is consistent.

value.text: Drinks alcohol occasionally, about two standard drinks a week.

release_text: Drinks alcohol occasionally, about two standard drinks a week.
lay_text: Just the odd glass of wine, maybe two a week.
rationale: Little alcohol keeps alcohol-related sideroblastic change an unlikely explanation (P4); GGT 13 U/L and MCV 93 fL fit.

value.text: Temperature 36.8 °C; pulse 104/min, regular; blood pressure 124/76 mmHg; respiratory rate 16/min; SpO2 98% on room air.

release_text: Temperature 36.8 °C; pulse 104/min, regular; blood pressure 124/76 mmHg; respiratory rate 16/min; SpO2 98% on room air.
rationale: G01: afebrile (CRP <0.4 mg/L); tachycardia from Hb 72 g/L; normal blood pressure and saturation. The ECG row uses a matching rate (102/min).

value.text: No cervical, axillary or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

release_text: No cervical, axillary or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

value.text: Gums and gum margins look normal.

value.text: Soft; mild diffuse tenderness without guarding or rebound; no masses; bowel sounds present.
